definition: Residual Networks (ResNet) are a type of convolutional neural network (CNN) where connections skip one or more layers.
details: Residual Networks (ResNet) are a type of convolutional neural network (CNN) where connections skip one or more layers. They are designed to enable training of extremely deep neural networks to achieve better performance.

explainer.lead: ResNet is a convolutional neural network whose connections skip one or more layers, designed so extremely deep networks can be trained to achieve better performance. Its 2015 release also popularized the residual connection across deep learning.

tiers.eli5: The network has shortcuts that let information jump over layers, so even a very tall stack of layers can still learn properly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers stack residual blocks x ↦ f(x) + x, which stabilizes training and convergence for networks hundreds of layers deep. A pitfall is assuming any use of the motif makes a model a ResNet; it is now a common motif in networks that are seemingly unrelated to ResNet.
tiers.paperLevel: A type of convolutional neural network where connections skip one or more layers; the residual connection is x ↦ f(x) + x for an arbitrary module f. It was developed in 2015 for image recognition and won ILSVRC that year.

explainer.example: A 2015 residual network trained on ImageNet won the ILSVRC, demonstrating that very deep CNNs with shortcut connections could train successfully.
